museumIntro: Push every crate onto a marked goal. You can push one crate at a time, but cannot pull it. Use all four arrow keys, U to undo a move and N for the next puzzle after solving one. In the lessons, you will write movement, pushing and completion rules, then build your own room from rows of tiles.

museumStory.title: 1982: a puzzle about moving boxes
museumStory.text:
Sokoban was created by Hiroyuki Imabayashi. Thinking Rabbit released it for Japanese home computers in December 1982, on cassette tape. It built a puzzle around an everyday task: moving boxes into the right places. The order of your moves matters because you can push a box into a position you cannot recover from.

Crate Cottage uses that box-pushing idea with original rooms. You can explore the rules, learn to implement them, or design a room of your own.
